stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy learns that a certified pharmacy technician's certification from the certifying body lapsed last week. The individual's Board pharmacy technician licence remains current. Which consequences follow? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The individual is limited to the duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician.
The individual must use the title pharmacy technician.
The individual is counted as a pharmacy technician when calculating supervisory ratios.
The individual may no longer work in the pharmacy in any capacity.
The individual's Board pharmacy technician licence is automatically suspended.

stem:
Case A: A technician's Massachusetts license remains active, but national certification expires. The technician continues using the CPhT title and is counted in a certified position for staffing.

Case B: The manager says no action is needed until the state technician license expires because national certification is a separate credential.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A lapsed national certificate automatically makes the active state license a revoked license.
The specified loss-of-certification reporting duty is separate from changing work assignments.
The technician must be treated within the ordinary technician duties and title while certification is lapsed.
The lapse changes the qualified category used in the supervisory-ratio calculation.

stem:
Case A: A nationally certified technician moves to Massachusetts but has not yet obtained a Massachusetts technician license. The pharmacy schedules dispensing support work immediately.

Case B: A manager labels a licensed technician as a pharmacist intern because the technician plans to enter pharmacy school next year.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: National certification does not replace the Massachusetts technician license.
A trainee may work without any Board license until the training is finished.
National technician certification transfers final dispensing validation to the technician.
An employer can create intern authority by changing the employee's job title.

stem:
Case A: A technician assumes that the Massachusetts license expires on the same December 31 cycle as the pharmacists in the pharmacy.

Case B: A technician sends a late renewal application after the birthday-based expiration and asks to continue working while it is processed.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The technician license expires on every even-numbered December 31.
A lapse exceeding two years is resolved solely by an employer competency sign-off.
A pending late renewal does not itself authorize practice under an expired license.
Paying the national-certification renewal fee also renews the state technician license.

stem:
Case A: A technician assumes that the Massachusetts license expires on the same December 31 cycle as the pharmacists in the pharmacy.

Case B: A technician sends a late renewal application after the birthday-based expiration and asks to continue working while it is processed.

choices.text: The technician license uses the stated biennial birthday-based expiration.
Renewal of national certification does not renew the state technician license.
A pending late renewal does not itself authorize practice under an expired license.
A lapse exceeding two years can involve additional Board conditions.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy has just learned that a staff member's technician certification lapsed. The staff member continues to wear a name tag reading Certified Pharmacy Technician while the pharmacy sorts out the paperwork. What should the pharmacy do about the name tag?

choices.text: Change the tag to read Pharmacy Technician.
Leave the tag unchanged until the certification is restored.
Remove the name tag entirely until the certification is restored.
Change the tag to read Pharmacy Technician Trainee.
Leave the tag unchanged if the pharmacist on duty documents the lapse.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician's license has been expired for 26 months. The technician submits the renewal form and fees, but the Board has not renewed the license or decided whether to impose additional conditions. The pharmacy wants the technician to begin work under direct pharmacist supervision. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: Submitting the form and fees restores the license provisionally while the Board reviews the application.
Direct pharmacist supervision may permit practice during the renewal review despite the expired license.
A lapse exceeding two years automatically requires a specified national technician examination before renewal.
The technician cannot practice until renewal; because the lapse exceeded two years, additional Board conditions may apply.

stem:
The compliance calendar has a row for a Massachusetts pharmacy technician license. The manager must use that license’s ordinary expiration cycle, not the renewal date of another credential.

Which calendar entry matches this credential? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The licensee’s birthdate in its two-year renewal cycle
December 31 of the even-numbered renewal year
December 31 every year
December 31 of the odd-numbered renewal year

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician telephones a prescriber's office for refill authorization. The office authorizes the refill but also increases the daily dose. The pharmacist on duty had approved the technician making refill calls. What should happen next?

choices.text: The technician may accept the change because the pharmacist pre-approved the call.
The technician may accept the change if she reads it back to the prescriber's agent.
The technician may accept the change and flag it for the pharmacist's final verification.
The technician may accept the change only if she is a certified pharmacy technician.
The technician may not accept the change because information has changed from the previous prescription.

stem:
Case A: An ordinary licensed technician, not a trainee and not nationally certified, receives a prescriber's unchanged Schedule IV refill authorization with pharmacist approval.

Case B: During another refill call, the prescriber changes the dose. The ordinary technician treats the call as the same unchanged-refill task.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Only a nationally certified technician may receive any unchanged verbal-refill authorization.
A dose change is not an unchanged refill authorization.
An employer's refill-call checklist independently grants the trainee the same authority.
The same refill authority extends to Schedule II because the prescriber called directly.

stem:
Case A: A prescriber calls with an unchanged refill authorization while the pharmacist is occupied. A technician trainee offers to receive the authorization.

Case B: A trainee is asked to telephone a prescriber and settle a dose discrepancy because the request seems routine.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Calling the prescriber makes clinical dose clarification permissible trainee work.
A trainee who can offer counseling may independently provide the clinical counseling.
Typing a proposed telephone order grants authority to accept it as a prescription.
The trainee is excluded from the permitted unchanged verbal-refill authorization role.

stem:

Case B: During another refill call, the prescriber changes the dose. The ordinary technician treats the call as the same unchanged-refill task.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The permitted unchanged verbal-refill pathway includes an ordinary licensed technician with the required supervision and approval.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is assigning staff to receive Schedule II stock. The pharmacist has approved written policies and procedures. Which statements correctly distinguish the current technician pathways? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A registered pharmacy technician may assist with transporting Schedule II stock under pharmacist supervision.
A registered pharmacy technician who is not certified may assist with Schedule II transport under pharmacist supervision but does not thereby gain the certified technician's broader handling role.
A certified pharmacy technician may assist with transporting and handling Schedule II stock under pharmacist supervision when the pharmacy's approved policies permit it.
A pharmacy technician trainee may independently assume Schedule II accountability because trainee registration is enough to replace pharmacist oversight.
The pharmacist remains responsible for Schedule II accountability, security, and professional judgment even when authorized support personnel assist.

stem:
Case A: A nationally certified, Massachusetts-licensed technician is asked to receive a new Schedule III prescription under pharmacist supervision and approval.

Case B: A prescriber then telephones an emergency Schedule II authorization and asks the same technician to receive it because the pharmacist is busy.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Emergency oral Schedule II follows the practitioner-to-pharmacist authorization pathway.
National certification alone supplies the state authority to receive new prescriptions.
The certified-technician scope is limited to unchanged refills and excludes new verbal Schedule III prescriptions.
The right to receive a verbal order includes independent adjustment of its dose.

stem:
Case A: A nationally certified, Massachusetts-licensed technician is asked to receive a new Schedule III prescription under pharmacist supervision and approval.

Case B: A prescriber then telephones an emergency Schedule II authorization and asks the same technician to receive it because the pharmacist is busy.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: National certification alone supplies the state authority to receive new prescriptions.
The certified-technician scope is limited to unchanged refills and excludes new verbal Schedule III prescriptions.
Receiving a permitted order does not authorize clinical modification of it.
Emergency oral Schedule II follows the practitioner-to-pharmacist authorization pathway.

stem:
Case A: For a proposed federal emergency oral Schedule II prescription, the prescriber's receptionist calls a certified technician instead of the prescribing practitioner speaking to the pharmacist.

Case B: A central-fill pharmacy proposes accepting the emergency oral prescription directly under the ordinary retail emergency pathway.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The federal emergency-oral provision does not allow the central-fill pharmacy to receive it through that pathway.
The specified federal emergency pathway requires the prescribing individual practitioner to authorize the pharmacist.
An unknown caller's assertion of being a prescriber removes the need for authenticity verification.
The pharmacist must promptly reduce the required oral information to a record.

stem:

Case B: A prescriber then telephones an emergency Schedule II authorization and asks the same technician to receive it because the pharmacist is busy.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: National certification alone supplies the state authority to receive new prescriptions.
The right to receive a verbal order includes independent adjustment of its dose.
Certification permits the technician to receive emergency oral Schedule II instead of the pharmacist.
The specified certified-technician scope includes new verbal Schedule III through VI prescriptions.

stem: A patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacy to obtain a prescription issued 13 months ago for a prescription-only drug that is not listed in Schedules I through V. The prescription record shows two authorized refills remaining. Which statements should the receiving pharmacist apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The remaining refills keep the prescription transferable until both have been dispensed.
The drug falls within Massachusetts Schedule VI because it is a prescription drug not otherwise placed in Schedules I through V.
The transfer must be declined because a Schedule VI prescription may not be transferred more than one year after issuance.
The transfer may proceed, but the receiving pharmacy must apply the federal six-month refill period for Schedule III through V prescriptions.
The rule allowing Schedule VI prescriptions to transfer in the same manner as Schedule III through V prescriptions does not displace the separate one-year transfer ceiling.

stem:
Case A: A certified technician is asked, with pharmacist approval, to transfer remaining authorized refills of a Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription.

Case B: The same employee is asked to transfer a Schedule IV refill between two independent pharmacies and assumes the Schedule VI personnel rule also applies.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Certified-technician prescription-transfer authority applies to every schedule.
An urgent patient request converts an ordinary technician into an authorized transfer pharmacist.
A technician-performed VI transfer creates a fresh year of validity.
The federal controlled-refill transfer requires the licensed-pharmacist communication pathway.

stem: A patient asks Pharmacy B to obtain a Massachusetts warfarin prescription from Pharmacy A. The prescription was issued 10 months ago and has three authorized refills remaining. Pharmacy B has a certified pharmacy technician available, and the pharmacist on duty approves the technician’s participation. Which statements are consistent with the current Massachusetts transfer framework? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacies should act on the patient’s transfer request in a timely manner rather than impose a blanket no-transfer rule.

A Schedule VI prescription may be transferred in the same manner as Schedule III-V prescriptions, and the remaining authorized refills may be transferred while the prescription is within the one-year limit.
A certified pharmacy technician may perform a Schedule VI prescription transfer when the pharmacist on duty approves the activity.
Massachusetts requires the transferring pharmacy to charge the patient a transfer fee before releasing the prescription.
The transfer is barred solely because the prescription is more than six months old, even though it was issued less than one year ago.

stem:
Case A: A certified technician is asked, with pharmacist approval, to transfer remaining authorized refills of a Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription.

Case B: The same employee is asked to transfer a Schedule IV refill between two independent pharmacies and assumes the Schedule VI personnel rule also applies.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A certified technician may substitute for the pharmacists in every federal III–V refill transfer.
A technician-performed VI transfer creates a fresh year of validity.
The specified certified-technician transfer authority is for Schedule VI prescriptions.
An urgent patient request converts an ordinary technician into an authorized transfer pharmacist.

stem:
A Schedule VI prescription from a Massachusetts practitioner is within one year of its original issue date and shows 1 authorized refills remaining. It has already been transferred once. The patient now requests another refill transfer. No emergency-continuity exception is claimed.

Which conclusion is correct? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The receiving pharmacy receives a new one-year prescription automatically.
The original one-year validity has ended; transfer cannot restart it.
There is no remaining refill authorization to transfer for this refill request.
A timely transfer may preserve the remaining authorized refills.

stem:
Case A: A never-filled Schedule III prescription originally received on paper is scanned, and staff attempt to use the original-unfilled-EPCS transfer rule.

Case B: A separate never-filled Schedule VI prescription originated on paper, and staff assume the controlled EPCS format restriction prohibits its Massachusetts transfer too.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Scanning does not qualify the first prescription as an originally electronic prescription for that pathway.
Authority to transfer Schedule VI necessarily includes authority to transfer Schedule III.
The Schedule VI transfer still needs valid time and remaining authorization conditions.
The described Massachusetts Schedule VI unfilled-transfer pathway is not restricted to electronic-origin prescriptions.

stem:
Case A: A never-filled Schedule III prescription originally received on paper is scanned, and staff attempt to use the original-unfilled-EPCS transfer rule.

Case B: A separate never-filled Schedule VI prescription originated on paper, and staff assume the controlled EPCS format restriction prohibits its Massachusetts transfer too.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Authority to transfer Schedule VI necessarily includes authority to transfer Schedule III.
The Schedule VI transfer still needs valid time and remaining authorization conditions.
Scanning does not qualify the first prescription as an originally electronic prescription for that pathway.
The described Massachusetts Schedule VI unfilled-transfer pathway is not restricted to electronic-origin prescriptions.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee is performing data-entry work while a pharmacist is directly supervising the trainee. At pickup, the patient asks whether the new medication can be taken with warfarin, and the profile shows an unresolved DUR alert. Which actions are appropriate for the trainee? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Collect and enter nonclinical demographic information while remaining under direct pharmacist supervision.
Counsel the patient on the interaction after reading the drug-information screen.
Perform authorized prescription-processing and staging tasks under direct pharmacist supervision, while leaving final verification to the pharmacist.
Continue other authorized clerical or technical trainee functions while under direct pharmacist supervision.
Refer the clinical question and unresolved DUR issue to the pharmacist rather than exercising pharmacist professional judgment.

stem:
Case A: A pharmacy proposes that a highly experienced certified technician complete final patient-specific prescription validation after a barcode scan.

Case B: An intern under direct pharmacist supervision counsels a patient, while a technician offers to resolve a drug-interaction alert independently.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A successful barcode scan authorizes the technician to perform final dispensing validation.
Delegating the offer necessarily delegates the counseling itself.
A properly supervised intern may counsel, but the technician may not independently resolve the clinical alert.
A certified technician's medication-history authority includes prescribing a replacement therapy.

stem:
At a Massachusetts community pharmacy, the pharmacist is on duty and available. Each proposed assignment below is evaluated with the employee’s current state license and certification. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacist performs final patient-specific prescription verification after an intern prepares the medication.
A supervised nationally certified technician counsels a patient about a newly prescribed inhaler.
A technician gathers a medication history and independently resolves the interaction by changing the dose.
A certified technician transfers an otherwise eligible Schedule IV prescription with pharmacist approval.
An external maintenance worker enters the prescription area while accompanied and monitored by a pharmacist.

stem:

choices.text: Final patient-specific dispensing validation remains the pharmacist's responsibility.
An offer of counseling may be conveyed by a trained designee without delegating actual counseling.
A properly supervised intern may counsel, but the technician may not independently resolve the clinical alert.

stem:
A licensed intern under direct pharmacist supervision has entered a new prescription, completed preparation, and counseled the patient. The pharmacist has not performed final dispensing verification.

What must occur before the prescription is released? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The intern may substitute a second barcode scan for pharmacist verification.
Another intern may independently verify the first intern's work.
Have the pharmacist perform final dispensing verification before release.
The pharmacist may postpone verification until the end-of-day reconciliation.

stem:
Case A: A trained cashier offers pharmacist counseling, but then personally answers a question about changing a dose because the line is long.

Case B: A properly supervised pharmacy intern is available to provide the clinical counseling, while the technician believes only the pharmacist may speak to the patient.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: National technician certification makes the technician an authorized clinical counselor.
Training to extend the offer also authorizes the cashier to decide dose changes during counseling.
The pharmacy must distinguish the offer, the patient's response, and any counseling actually provided.
A supervised intern is prohibited from all patient counseling under the described rule.

stem:
Case A: A pharmacy proposes that a highly experienced certified technician complete final patient-specific prescription validation after a barcode scan.

Case B: An intern under direct pharmacist supervision counsels a patient, while a technician offers to resolve a drug-interaction alert independently.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A properly supervised intern may counsel, but the technician may not independently resolve the clinical alert.
Final patient-specific dispensing validation remains the pharmacist's responsibility.
An offer of counseling may be conveyed by a trained designee without delegating actual counseling.

stem:
Case A: A trained cashier offers pharmacist counseling, but then personally answers a question about changing a dose because the line is long.

Case B: A properly supervised pharmacy intern is available to provide the clinical counseling, while the technician believes only the pharmacist may speak to the patient.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A technician cannot replace the authorized counselor by providing the clinical explanation.
An appropriately supervised intern may provide the counseling described in the notes.
Documenting the offer necessarily proves that clinical counseling was completed.

stem:

Case B: The manager treats this transport task as authority for the same ordinary technician to perform unrestricted Schedule II vault work.

choices.text: All Schedule II formulations necessarily have identical technician-handling permissions.

stem: At an eligible Massachusetts hospital ADD, evaluate each stocking action independently. Which are permitted under the current technician stocking policy? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A PTT loads pharmacist-verified alprazolam with electronic validation under pharmacist direction/supervision

stem:

Case B: One technician finds a discrepancy and edits the balance without involving the MOR or the designated pharmacist.

choices.text: A discrepancy adjustment follows the MOR or authorized pharmacist-designee pathway.
Only an unlicensed inventory vendor may make routine electronic inventory entries.
Using two certified technicians removes the required pharmacist verification of the count.

stem:
At a Massachusetts community pharmacy, the pharmacist is on duty and available. Each proposed assignment below is evaluated with the employee’s current state license and certification. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which ONE proposed handling is supported by the applicable requirements?

choices.text: A certified technician makes a permitted Schedule II perpetual-inventory entry subject to the pharmacy’s controls.
A licensed technician without national certification accepts a new verbal prescription for gabapentin with pharmacist approval.
An intern performs final patient-specific prescription verification because the supervising pharmacist is nearby.

stem:

Case B: One technician finds a discrepancy and edits the balance without involving the MOR or the designated pharmacist.

choices.text: An unexplained difference requires investigation rather than a silent numerical correction.

stem:
A certified technician enters a documented CII receipt and then finds an unexplained two-tablet discrepancy. The MOR is present.

Which next action respects the distinction between entry and adjustment? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Delete and reenter the receipt until the computer matches the count.
Offset the difference against tomorrow's anticipated dispensing.
Refer the discrepancy to the MOR for investigation and adjustment.
Reduce the balance by two under the receipt-entry authority.

stem: A nationally certified Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy technician is using the special ADD stocking pathway without prior pharmacist verification. Which conditions must be satisfied? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The medication is non-patient-specific Schedule VI stock
The medication is not a PMP drug such as gabapentin
Barcode scanning or other electronic validation is used
Transfer qualifying stock in manufacturer-sealed or original packaging without further manipulation.
The same no-prior-verification shortcut extends to Schedule V because the technician is nationally certified

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is scheduling a shift and wants to work with four support personnel assisting in filling prescriptions. Which staffing combinations satisfy the minimum supervisory ratio? Select all that apply.

choices.text: One certified pharmacy technician, one pharmacy intern and two pharmacy technicians.
Two certified pharmacy technicians and two pharmacy technician trainees.
One pharmacy intern, one pharmacy technician and two pharmacy technician trainees.
Four pharmacy technicians whose licences are all current.
One certified pharmacy technician and three pharmacy technician trainees.

stem:

choices.text: The one-to-four rule requires an intern even when two certified technicians are present.
A compliant one-to-four ratio permits ordinary technicians to perform final verification.

stem:

Case B: One of the ordinary technicians is replaced by a licensed intern. The manager reviews both the staffing ratio and the intern's permitted tasks.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Calling a filling technician an inventory specialist automatically removes the person from the ratio.
The stated one-to-three pathway requires at least one intern or certified technician.

stem:

Case B: The scheduler substitutes an ordinary technician for the intern, leaving one certified technician and three ordinary technicians in the four-person group.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The one-to-four rule requires an intern even when two certified technicians are present.
Any single certified technician qualifies a four-person support group.
The first group satisfies a listed one-to-four qualifying-category combination.
A compliant one-to-four ratio permits ordinary technicians to perform final verification.

stem:
Case A: One pharmacist is scheduled with four prescription-filling support personnel: one certified technician, one intern, and two ordinary technicians.

Case B: The scheduler substitutes an ordinary technician for the intern, leaving one certified technician and three ordinary technicians in the four-person group.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A compliant one-to-four ratio permits ordinary technicians to perform final verification.
The first group satisfies a listed one-to-four qualifying-category combination.
One certified technician with three ordinary technicians does not satisfy the stated one-to-four combinations.
Two certified technicians can satisfy the qualifying component of a four-person group.

stem:
Case A: One pharmacist supervises three ordinary technicians who assist with prescription preparation. No intern or certified technician is in the group.

Case B: One of the ordinary technicians is replaced by a licensed intern. The manager reviews both the staffing ratio and the intern's permitted tasks.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The stated one-to-three pathway requires at least one intern or certified technician.
Personnel who actually assist professional filling must be classified under the applicable ratio.
Expired certification cannot be counted as a currently certified staffing position.
A qualifying licensed intern can satisfy that category component without changing the other workers' scope.

stem:
Case A: One pharmacist supervises three ordinary technicians who assist with prescription preparation. No intern or certified technician is in the group.

Case B: One of the ordinary technicians is replaced by a licensed intern. The manager reviews both the staffing ratio and the intern's permitted tasks.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The original hiring credential remains sufficient after certification expires.
Three ordinary technicians satisfy the one-to-three qualifying-category condition.
A qualifying licensed intern can satisfy that category component without changing the other workers' scope.
Calling a filling technician an inventory specialist automatically removes the person from the ratio.

stem: During a busy evening shift a Massachusetts pharmacy intern, who is working under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor, is asked to oversee two pharmacy technicians who are filling prescriptions. Which statement best describes what the regulation permits?

choices.text: The intern may not oversee technicians until licensed as a pharmacist.
The intern may oversee technicians only if the preceptor leaves the pharmacy.
The intern may oversee technicians only after 1500 internship hours.
The intern may supervise pharmacy technicians while remaining under direct preceptor supervision.
The intern may oversee technicians only in an institutional pharmacy setting.

stem:
Case A: One pharmacist supervises three ordinary technicians who assist with prescription preparation. No intern or certified technician is in the group.

Case B: One of the ordinary technicians is replaced by a licensed intern. The manager reviews both the staffing ratio and the intern's permitted tasks.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The stated one-to-three pathway requires at least one intern or certified technician.
A qualifying licensed intern can satisfy that category component without changing the other workers' scope.
Expired certification cannot be counted as a currently certified staffing position.
Calling a filling technician an inventory specialist automatically removes the person from the ratio.

stem:
Case A: One pharmacist is scheduled with four prescription-filling support personnel: one certified technician, one intern, and two ordinary technicians.

Case B: The scheduler substitutes an ordinary technician for the intern, leaving one certified technician and three ordinary technicians in the four-person group.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The one-to-four rule requires an intern even when two certified technicians are present.
Meeting the staffing ratio does not grant a worker additional clinical duties.
The first group satisfies a listed one-to-four qualifying-category combination.
One certified technician with three ordinary technicians does not satisfy the stated one-to-four combinations.

stem:
A Massachusetts technician’s national certification expires on October 12, 2026. The Massachusetts technician license remains active. The technician tells the MOR the same day and plans to seek recertification. The pharmacy has not submitted a report to the Massachusetts Board.

Which steps are required by the cited certification-loss rules? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Keep the certified-technician title during a 14-day reporting grace period.
Report the loss of certification to the Board within 14 calendar days.
Treat the active Massachusetts technician license as automatically revoked.
Defer the Board report until the next Massachusetts technician-license renewal.
Use the pharmacy-technician title and category while certification is lapsed.

stem:
A technician returns to Massachusetts after a career break. The state technician license expired more than two years ago, but national certification is current. The technician asks whether the pharmacist rule requiring MPJE after a long lapse automatically applies to a technician.

Which statement accurately describes the technician’s renewal rule? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: MPJE is automatically required whenever any pharmacy-related license lapses for two years.
Current national certification authorizes work while the state renewal application is processed.
An employer’s competency sign-off removes additional Board conditions for this lapse.
The Board may impose additional conditions; the technician rule does not itself mandate MPJE.

stem:
A prescriber’s agent calls to authorize another refill of an existing Schedule VI prescription. The drug, strength, directions, and other prescription information are unchanged. A licensed noncertified technician and a licensed technician trainee are available; the pharmacist on duty can approve the assignment.

Who may receive this unchanged refill authorization under the stated personnel rules? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The licensed technician, with the pharmacist’s approval for the assignment.
The trainee, if the pharmacist directly supervises the telephone conversation.
Either employee, because the pharmacist will verify the product before dispensing.
Neither employee; a pharmacist must personally receive every unchanged refill authorization.

stem:
A prescriber telephones a new Schedule VI prescription. The pharmacist on duty approves a Massachusetts-licensed technician with current national certification to receive the call. The prescriber supplies the drug, strength, directions, quantity, and other required information. No therapeutic clarification is needed.

Which workflow is consistent with the technician’s scope? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Route the call to the pharmacist because technician telephone authority is limited to unchanged refills.
Have the technician identify as certified and receive the order for pharmacist review.
Have the technician receive the order and complete its final dispensing verification.
Have the technician complete the clinical review because the prescriber supplied every required field.

stem:
A noncertified technician with an active Massachusetts license routinely takes filled, pharmacist-verified Schedule II prescriptions to the pickup counter. Today the pharmacist asks the technician to open a stock bottle of methylphenidate tablets and count a new prescription. The pharmacist will perform the final check, and written procedures permit the technician to assist with CII transport.

Which assignment respects the technician’s current scope? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Keep the technician on transport and have the pharmacist count the tablets.
Let the technician count before the pharmacist performs the final check.
Authorize the technician to count by amending the written transport procedure.
Have two ordinary technicians count together and sign the worksheet.

stem:
Case A: A pharmacy uses DEA Form 106 as though it were the ordering document for an ordinary Schedule II stock purchase.

Case B: The pharmacy returns eligible Schedule II stock to an authorized supplier and assumes the return eliminates all applicable ordering and transaction records.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Form 106 is the ordinary Schedule II stock-ordering document.
Expiration removes the controlled status and all inventory responsibility immediately.
A registrant stock return must follow its applicable Part 1305 and transaction-record requirements.
A patient return is not the same as a registrant's stock return.

stem:
The MOR is away for three days and has designated the pharmacist on duty to cover inventory adjustments. Two Massachusetts-licensed technicians with current national certification conduct the CII perpetual-inventory count for oxycodone tablets under written procedures. The team finds that a receipt was entered twice, and the pharmacist confirms the cause from the source records.

Which steps fit the permitted workflow? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Accept the two technicians’ signatures as a substitute for pharmacist verification of the completed count.
Have the supervising pharmacist verify that the count was completed in accordance with Board requirements.
Let either technician correct the balance using the authority to enter CII receipt transactions.
Treat the MOR’s return as a prerequisite for any discrepancy adjustment.
Have the pharmacist designee make the discrepancy adjustment and report the change to the MOR.

stem:
A pharmacy is not providing vaccination services. One pharmacist supervises a filling team of one currently certified technician and three noncertified technicians, all with active Massachusetts technician licenses. A second currently certified technician is assigned only to placing pharmacist-verified compliance packages into delivery totes, with that role identified on the posted schedule.

Which reassignment meets the ordinary ratio without adding another pharmacist? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Exchange the tote worker's assignment with one ordinary filling technician and post both revised roles.
Keep the filling assignments and use both certified employees to satisfy the four-person team's qualifying mix.
Add the tote worker to the filling team while keeping the four current workers on prescription preparation.
Reduce the filling team to three ordinary technicians by moving its certified technician to the tote station.
